description:
Boat-billed Flycatcher perched high up in a tree in the rainforest near Canopy Camp in Darien province, Panama.

Boat-billed Flycatcher (Megarynchus pitangua) Large flycatcher of tropical and subtropical forest and woodland, and in semi-open areas with taller trees. Perches mainly at mid-upper levels, often in the canopy. Differs from Great Kiskadee, which prefers more open and less wooded habitats. Boat-billed Flycatcher has dull olive upperparts and lacks the bright rusty wings and tail of Great Kiskadee. It also has a stouter bill, with a more strongly arched ridge along the top. There are several subspecies.
